text:
mia: Heads-up — multiple customers reported mass deprovision after last night's RBAC rename. Saw a bunch of SCIM deprov spikes and KMS decrypt errors in the provisioner logs. Can we triage?
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-153 - SCIM deprovision loop (P1) — channel: #eng-security :rotating_light:
sanjay: I pulled logs from scim-provisioner-3, looks like KMS ops failing on decrypt for extid blobs. snippet:```
2026-03-22T21:11:02Z scim-provisioner-3 ERROR deprovision userId=acct_ABC err="kms:Decrypt failed: NotFound"
2026-03-22T21:11:02Z scim-provisioner-3 WARN reconcile userId=acct_DEF externalId_mismatch=true
```
elaine: Audit pipeline shows very few scim.deprovision events for the time window. Either the deprov path bypassed audit (bad) or our pipeline filter dropped them. Query I ran: `SELECT count(*) FROM audit_events WHERE event_type='scim.deprovision' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-22T21:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-22T22:00:00Z';` returned 3 while customer reports imply hundreds.
jordan: Pausing auto-deprovision jobs now — `scimctl pause deprovision --env prod` done. Stopped new jobs, existing queued workers will finish. :white_check_mark:
sanjay: Preliminary hypothesis: yesterday's KMS alias rotation + the RBAC rename together caused externalId rewrite mismatch. SCIM sees user extid != provisioning mapping -> treat as orphan -> deprov. KMS decrypt NotFound implies alias mapping changed.
mia: Assigning owners: @sanjay for KMS/key mapping, @elaine for audit pipeline validation, @jordan for provisioning hold and rollback options. ETA 2h for initial mitigation steps. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
devex-bot: FYI — related deploy: rbac-service commit 7f4d3b deployed 03:12Z added `role_name_normalize` which renamed some role strings (e.g. "developer" -> "dev"). Migration ran with `--rewrite-roles` flag.
elaine: I dug into the RBAC migration logs — the role rename job also rewrote the internal subject records but did NOT include `external_id` in the rewrite batch due to a missing join. That explains phishing the SCIM key lookups.
sanjay: Workaround options:
- revert KMS alias mapping to previous alias (fast but touches keys)
- re-run RBAC migration with `--preserve-extid` to keep external IDs intact then requeue a SCIM reconcile
I prefer re-run migration on staging first. Command I plan to test: `./scripts/rbac-migrate --preserve-extid --dry-run`
mia: Agreed. Do it in staging, validate with synthetic tenant and a small cohort. If it passes, schedule a hotfix migration in prod with a maintenance window. Notify customers and support.
jordan: If migration is slow we can also run a targeted SCIM reconciliation for affected tenants: `scimctl reconcile --tenant TENANT_ID --mode dry-run` then commit.
sanjay: KMS team — pinging @keyops for alias history. Need to confirm whether alias rotation happened around 03:10Z and whether tombstone keys exist.
ops-bot: Incident updated: P1 -> mitigated (auto-deprovision paused). Next update planned in 45m.
elaine: For audit gap, I'll re-run ingestion with relaxed filters and backfill missing scim.deprovision events from raw kafka topic. If we find deprov events there, we'll attach to the incident for downstream customer comms.
mia: Good plan. Post any rollout decisions here before touching prod. Thanks all.
devex-bot: Note added to thread: potential root cause = combination of RBAC role string rewrite + KMS alias rotation causing externalId lookup failures (leading to orphan detection).
sanjay: Starting staging rehearsal now. Will post dry-run outputs.
mia: thx, keep this thread updated.
